cases.sentence: И первое ___, попавшееся ему на ступеньках большой лестницы, был Облонский.
cases.translation: And the first face that caught his eye on the steps of the great staircase was Oblonsky's.
cases.explain: Лицо is the grammatical subject of был (was), so it stands in the nominative case.

cases.sentence: Приближение ___ все более и более обозначалось движением приготовлений на станции.
cases.translation: The approach of the train was becoming more and more evident from the bustle of preparations at the station.
cases.explain: Поезда shows what the approach belongs to (the approach OF the train), a noun-complement genitive.

cases.sentence: по ___ своему, не мог себе представить других к матери отношений.
cases.translation: by his upbringing, he could not imagine any other kind of relations toward his mother.
cases.explain: The preposition по (according to) governs the dative case.

cases.sentence: Вронский выехал на ___ Петербургской железной дороги встречать мать.
cases.translation: Vronsky drove out to the station of the Petersburg railway to meet his mother.
cases.explain: The preposition на (to) with a verb of motion governs the accusative case.

cases.sentence: прокатился паровоз с медленно и мерно насупливающимся и растягивающимся ___ среднего колеса.
cases.translation: the engine rolled past with the slowly, evenly working piston-rod of its middle wheel.
cases.explain: The preposition с (with) expressing an accompanying feature governs the instrumental case.

cases.sentence: Слова кондуктора разбудили его и заставили вспомнить о матери и предстоящем ___ с ней.
cases.translation: The conductor's words woke him and made him remember his mother and the upcoming meeting with her.
cases.explain: The preposition о (about) governs the prepositional case.

reading.ru: На другой день в одиннадцать часов утра Вронский выехал на станцию Петербургской железной дороги встречать мать.
reading.question: Where did Vronsky go at eleven o'clock the next morning?
options: To the Petersburg railway station to meet his mother
reading.correct: To the Petersburg railway station to meet his mother
reading.explain: The text says he drove out to the station of the Petersburg railway to meet his mother.

reading.ru: И первое лицо, попавшееся ему на ступеньках большой лестницы, был Облонский, ожидавший с этим же поездом сестру.
reading.question: Who was the first person Vronsky encountered at the station?
options: Oblonsky, waiting for his sister on the same train
Levin, about to leave for the country
reading.correct: Oblonsky, waiting for his sister on the same train
reading.explain: The text says the first face he saw was Oblonsky's, who was waiting for his sister on the same train.

reading.question: How did Oblonsky jokingly answer when asked whom he was meeting?
options: That he was meeting a pretty woman
That he was meeting his mother
That he was meeting a business partner
That he was meeting no one in particular
reading.correct: That he was meeting a pretty woman
reading.explain: Oblonsky jokes «Я? Я хорошенькую женщину» — he says he is meeting a pretty woman (his sister).

reading.question: Whom did Vronsky realize Oblonsky was actually meeting?
reading.explain: Vronsky says «Ах, это Каренину» once he learns the sister's name is Karenina.

reading.ru: Но Алексея Александровича, моего знаменитого зятя, верно знаешь?
reading.question: Whom does Oblonsky ask Vronsky if he knows, describing him as his famous brother-in-law?
reading.explain: Oblonsky asks about Алексей Александрович, his famous brother-in-law, i.e. Karenin.

reading.ru: «Ну что ж, в воскресенье сделаем ужин для Дивы», — сказал он ему
reading.question: What plan does Vronsky mention to Oblonsky regarding Sunday?
reading.explain: Vronsky says they will arrange a supper for the diva («ужин для Дивы») on Sunday.

reading.question: How does Oblonsky describe Levin to Vronsky?
reading.explain: Oblonsky says «Он славный, малый» — that Levin is a fine, good fellow.

reading.ru: Или он вчера сделал предложение твоей свояченице?
reading.question: What does Oblonsky hint may have happened between Levin and Kitty?
options: That Levin proposed to his sister-in-law (Kitty) yesterday
That Levin quarreled with Kitty's father
That Levin left Moscow for good
That Levin had already married someone else
reading.correct: That Levin proposed to his sister-in-law (Kitty) yesterday
reading.explain: Oblonsky asks whether Levin made a proposal to his свояченица (sister-in-law), meaning Kitty.

reading.ru: Он так давно влюблен, и мне его очень жаль.
reading.question: How does Oblonsky feel about Levin's long-standing love?
reading.explain: Oblonsky says Levin has been in love for so long, and he feels very sorry for him (мне его очень жаль).

reading.ru: Я думаю, впрочем, что она может рассчитывать на лучшую партию, — сказал Вронский
reading.question: What does Vronsky say about Kitty's marriage prospects?
options: That she could count on a better match
That she should marry Levin immediately
That she has no good prospects at all
That he personally intends to marry her
reading.correct: That she could count on a better match
reading.explain: Vronsky remarks that he thinks she could count on a better match than Levin.

reading.ru: То, что он сейчас узнал про Китти, возбуждало и радовало его.
reading.question: How did the news about Kitty affect Vronsky?
reading.explain: The text says what he had just learned about Kitty excited and gladdened him.

reading.ru: «Графиня Вронская в этом отделении», — сказал молодцеватый кондуктор, подходя к Вронскому.
reading.question: What did the conductor tell Vronsky, reminding him of his purpose at the station?
options: That Countess Vronskaya was in that compartment
That the train had been delayed
That his mother had missed the train
That he needed to buy a new ticket
reading.correct: That Countess Vronskaya was in that compartment
reading.explain: The conductor tells him «Графиня Вронская в этом отделении», reminding him his mother had arrived.
